Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
value.conclusion: For every t>0, e(·,t) is absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n, E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=0. In addition E(s)=E(t) for all s,t>0; no assertion at time zero is made.

hypotheses.statement: u:ℝ^n × (0,∞) → ℝ^m is jointly C^∞ (smooth) on this open domain.
For every x∈ℝ^n and every t>0, |u(x,t)|=1.
For every x∈ℝ^n and every t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of a selected scalar field is assumed.
For every pair of real times 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact C⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

definitions.definition: u_tt(x,t)=∂u_t(x,t)/∂t, the componentwise second time derivative.

definitions.type: spatial derivative matrix field on ℝ^n × (0,∞)

e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². Norms and dot products throughout are Euclidean; all spatial integrals are Lebesgue integrals, written dx. Write e_t for the time partial derivative of e.
E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t) dx, the finite real Lebesgue integral, with exactly the normalization in the exercise (no factor 1/2).

value.representation_notes: Use n,m : ℕ with H001 retaining positivity; these index precisely the positive integer dimensions of the source. X n = Fin n → ℝ is the Cartesian coordinate model of ℝ^n. Its standard product topology and finite-dimensional derivative structure agree with the usual Euclidean structure, although its norm instance is the sup norm; no spatial Euclidean norm enters any source formula. Its volume is the product of one-dimensional Lebesgue measures, as defined by MeasureSpace.pi. V m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) = PiLp 2 (fun _ => ℝ), so its norm and inner ℝ are exactly the Euclidean norm and dot product. Fin n labels coordinates 0,...,n-1, corresponding bijectively to source coordinates 1,...,n; all sums range over every coordinate. u is an arbitrary total extension to X n × ℝ; H002 and all pointwise conclusions concern only the open set t>0. Every source positive-time function admits such an extension, and restriction recovers the source; derivative locality makes its nonpositive-time values irrelevant. H002 uses the inclusion of (⊤ : ℕ∞) into WithTop ℕ∞: this is the smoothness index, not the outer top, which would require analyticity. dt is the ordinary vector derivative in time; dx applies the spatial Fréchet derivative to Pi.single j 1, the jth unit coordinate vector, and repeated dx/dt give precisely the prescribed componentwise derivatives. density has no 1/2 factor. energy is Mathlib's total real Bochner integral; T004 establishes absolute integrability before its finite-energy meaning is used in T007 or any subsequent step. No integrability or differentiability is assumed by these definitions. sectionGood, supportGeometry and supportSections only package explicit N002 clauses as predicates and do not assert them. All positive-order joint derivatives are encoded by iteratedFDeriv ℝ (k+1); under smoothness this is equivalent to vanishing of all positive-order componentwise partial derivatives. H003 is retained although unused by the supplied route. M001–M004 are implemented by direct library use, not additional premise ports; Audit A notes remain local references. The only coordinate-view change actually needed is the insertion of one coordinate in R004; T008 proves the corresponding restricted integral identity before T009 uses it.

import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory Set Filter
open scoped BigOperators Topology

namespace WaveMap

abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ
abbrev V (m : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)

def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}
def box (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)
def openBox (n : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Set (X n) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Ioo (-R) R)
def slab (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

noncomputable def dt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def dx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => u (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)
noncomputable def lap {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
  fun p => ∑ j : Fin n, dx (dx u j) j p
noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => ‖dt u p‖ ^ 2 + ∑ j : Fin n, ‖dx u j p‖ ^ 2
noncomputable def densityT {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => density u (p.1, r)) p.2
noncomputable def energy {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x : X n, density u (x, t)
noncomputable def timeProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dt (dt u) p)
noncomputable def mixedProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dx u j p) (dx (dt u) j p)
noncomputable def lapProduct {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx (dx u j) j p)
noncomputable def flux {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => inner ℝ (dt u p) (dx u j p)
noncomputable def fluxDx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
    X n × ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => flux u j (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)

def sectionGood {n : ℕ} (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) (f : X n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ (∀ x, x ∉ C → f x = 0) ∧
  (∃ B : ℝ, 0 ≤ B ∧ ∀ x ∈ box n R, |f x| ≤ B) ∧ Integrable f

def supportGeometry {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (q : V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsCompact C ∧ 0 < R ∧ C ⊆ openBox n R ∧
  (∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ slab t, u (x, r) = q) ∧
  volume (box n R) = ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * R) ^ n) ∧
  volume (box n R) < ⊤ ∧
  (∀ k : ℕ, ∀ x, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ (k + 1) u (x, r) = 0)

def supportSections {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t : ℝ) (C : Set (X n)) (R : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ r ∈ interior (slab t),
    sectionGood C R (fun x => density u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => densityT u (x, r)) ∧
    sectionGood C R (fun x => timeProduct u (x, r)) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin n,
      sectionGood C R (fun x => mixedProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => lapProduct u j (x, r)) ∧
      sectionGood C R (fun x => fluxDx u j (x, r)))

noncomputable def quotient {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m)
    (t h : ℝ) (x : X n) : ℝ :=
  (density u (x, t + h) - density u (x, t)) / h

abbrev Other {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) := {i : Fin n // i ≠ j}
def insertCoord {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (y : Other j → ℝ) (z : ℝ) : X n :=
  fun i => if h : i = j then z else y ⟨i, h⟩
def otherBox {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) (R : ℝ) : Set (Other j → ℝ) :=
  Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)

end WaveMap

P.explanation: Positive integer dimensions are represented by n,m : ℕ with H001 : 1≤n ∧ 1≤m, a bijective encoding. X n is the usual real Cartesian coordinate space with product Lebesgue measure; V m has exactly the Euclidean norm and dot product. Fin n reindexes all n coordinates without changing finite sums. 1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
171: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
172: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
173: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
174: Neither proves external publications in Lean or

1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.
118: 
119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.

argument.text: Fix x∈ℝ^n and t>0. H001 gives positive finite dimensions and H002 permits all derivatives used here. By H004, u·u=1. Differentiation in time, by the ordinary product rule for the finite component sum defining the dot product, gives 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Choose the pointwise scalar a from H005. Then u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses no derivative or regularity of a.

Twice differentiating u·u=1 in time gives 2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt=0. For an arbitrary coordinate j0∈{1,...,n}, twice differentiating in x_{j0} similarly gives 2|∂_{x_{j0}}u|²+2u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=0. Thus u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=−|∂_{x_{j0}}u|². Generalize j0 over the spatial coordinates. Dot the normality equation for a with u and use |u|²=1. Finite distributivity and the definition of Δ_xu give a=u·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². The same calculation applies to every scalar satisfying that pointwise equation.

argument.text: F001 proves the two orthogonality identities at the arbitrary point. By F002 substitute the computed value of a into the pointwise normality equation from H005 to obtain u_tt−Δ_xu=(Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u. The scalar was chosen only at this point and is eliminated; it is not promoted to a regular scalar field. Generalizing x and t proves all the asserted pointwise identities.

argument.text: Choose such a compact C from F001. Compact subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space are bounded: for example the increasing family of open boxes with positive integral radii covers C, and a finite subcover puts C in one such box. Enlarging its radius if needed gives a positive radius with strict containment in the open box. This also covers C empty.

Choose R as in F002 and set Q=[−R,R]^n. Its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞. The complement of compact C is open. On the open set (ℝ^n∖C)×int J the map u is the constant q by F001. H002 implies that all positive-order derivatives vanish on that open set. Thus at interior times e, e_t and the products u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every j vanish outside C. Products and finite sums of smooth derivatives are continuous; in particular e and e_t are jointly continuous on the original open space-time domain.

argument.text: At any r∈int J, each spatial function in question is continuous, hence Lebesgue measurable, and bounded on compact Q. Its absolute value is bounded by a finite nonnegative constant times the indicator of Q, since it vanishes outside C⊂Q. The integral of that bound is the constant times (2R)^n, which is finite. This proves absolute integrability of e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every spatial index j. 1: # Conservation of energy for a sphere-valued wave map
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Lawrence C. Evans, *Partial Differential Equations*, second edition,
6: Graduate Studies in Mathematics 19, AMS, 2010, section 12.6, exercise 14,
7: printed page 694. The preceding exercise 13 defines the sphere-valued
8: wave map. ISBN: 978-0-8218-4974-3.
9: 
10: > 14. Prove that if \(\mathbf u\) is a wave map into the unit sphere,
11: > with compact support in space, we have conservation of energy:
12: > \[
13: > \frac{d}{dt}\int_{\mathbb R^n}
14: >       |\mathbf u_t|^2+|D\mathbf u|^2\,dx=0.
15: > \]
16: 
17: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
18: 
19: A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
20: the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
21: of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
22: This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
23: correction.
24: 
25: Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
26: \(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
27: Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:
28: 
29: 1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
30: 2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
31:    \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
32:    \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
33:    assumed.
34: 3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
35:    \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
36:    \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).
37: 
38: With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define
39: 
40: \[
41: e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
42: \qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
43: \]
44: 
45: The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
46: \(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
47: Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
48: and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.
49: 
50: ## Fixed natural-language proof
51: 
52: ### 1. Tangency and the wave-map equation
53: 
54: Differentiate \(u\cdot u=1\) in time. The product rule gives
55: \(2u\cdot u_t=0\), so
56: 
57: \[
58: u\cdot u_t=0,\qquad
59: u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)=a(u_t\cdot u)=0.          \tag{1}
60: \]
61: 
62: No derivative of \(a\) is needed. The familiar explicit equation also
63: follows from the assumptions: twice differentiating the unit constraint
64: gives \(u\cdot u_{tt}=-|u_t|^2\) and
65: \(u\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u=-|\partial_{x_j}u|^2\).
66: Dotting the normality equation with \(u\), using \(|u|^2=1\), yields
67: \(a=\sum_j|\partial_{x_j}u|^2-|u_t|^2\). This is a consequence,
68: not an additional PDE assumption.
69: 
70: ### 2. Common compact support and integrability
71: 
72: Fix \(t_0>0\), put \(J=[t_0/2,3t_0/2]\), and choose its compact
73: spatial set \(C\) from assumption 3. Since \(C\) is bounded, choose
74: \(R>0\) with \(C\subset(-R,R)^n\) and set \(Q=[-R,R]^n\).
75: The box has finite Lebesgue measure \((2R)^n\).
76: 
77: On the open set \((\mathbb R^n\setminus C)\times\operatorname{int}J\),
78: the map equals the constant \(q\), so all its positive-order
79: derivatives vanish. At interior times, \(e\), \(e_t\), and the
80: derivative products used below consequently vanish outside \(C\).
81: They are continuous by smoothness; their spatial sections are measurable,
82: bounded on \(Q\), and supported there. Their absolute integrals are
83: bounded by a finite constant times \(|Q|\). This proves integrability
84: of \(e(\cdot,t_0)\) and of all later terms. Since \(t_0\) was arbitrary,
85: the energy is a finite, well-defined integral at every positive time.
86: 
87: ### 3. Differentiate the energy integral
88: 
89: The product rule and equality of mixed derivatives give
90: 
91: \[
92: e_t=2u_t\cdot u_{tt}
93:    +2\sum_{j=1}^n\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t.           \tag{2}
94: \]
95: 
96: Choose \(\eta>0\) so that
97: \([t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\subset\operatorname{int}J\).
98: Continuity of (2) on the compact box
99: \(Q\times[t_0-\eta,t_0+\eta]\) gives a finite bound \(|e_t|\leq B\).
100: For \(0<|h|<\eta\), the one-variable mean value theorem at fixed
101: \(x\) therefore gives
102: 
103: \[
104: \left|\frac{e(x,t_0+h)-e(x,t_0)}h\right|
105: \leq B\mathbf1_Q(x).
106: \]
107: 
108: Outside \(Q\), both densities vanish, so the bound holds throughout
109: \(\mathbb R^n\). The right side is integrable. The difference
110: quotients converge pointwise to \(e_t(x,t_0)\). Dominated convergence
111: and linearity for these integrable functions now prove
112: 
113: \[
114: E'(t_0)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e_t(x,t_0)\,dx.            \tag{3}
115: \]
116: 
117: This establishes differentiability of the actual finite integral.

460: /-- A function is continuously differentiable up to `n` on `s` if, for any point `x` in `s`, it
461: admits continuous derivatives up to order `n` on a neighborhood of `x` in `s`.
462: The parameter `n` belongs to `ℕ∞ω` (accessible in the `ContDiff` scope), i.e. it can be a natural
463: number, `∞`, or `ω`.
464: 
465: For `n = ∞`, we only require that this holds up to any finite order (where the neighborhood may
466: depend on the finite order we consider).
467: For `n = ω`, we require the function to be analytic within `s` at every point of `s`. The precise
468: definition we give (all the derivatives should be analytic) is more involved to work around issues
469: when the space is not complete, but it is equivalent when the space is complete.
470: -/

53: in general. In the usual situations, they coincide with the usual definitions.
54: 
55: ### Definition of `C^n` functions in domains
56: 
57: One could define `C^n` functions in a domain `s` by fixing an arbitrary choice of derivatives (this
58: is what we do with `iteratedFDerivWithin`) and requiring that all these derivatives up to `n` are
59: continuous. If the derivative is not unique, this could lead to strange behavior like two `C^n`
60: functions `f` and `g` on `s` whose sum is not `C^n`. A better definition is thus to say that a
61: function is `C^n` inside `s` if it admits a sequence of derivatives up to `n` inside `s`.
62: 
63: This definition still has the problem that a function which is locally `C^n` would not need to
64: be `C^n`, as different choices of sequences of derivatives around different points might possibly
65: not be glued together to give a globally defined sequence of derivatives. (Note that this issue
66: cannot happen over the real numbers, thanks to partitions of unity, but the behavior over a general
67: field is not so clear, and we want a definition for general fields). Also, there are locality
68: problems for the order parameter: one could image a function which, for each `n`, has a nice
69: sequence of derivatives up to order `n`, but they do not coincide for varying `n` and can therefore
70: not be glued to give rise to an infinite sequence of derivatives. This would give a function
71: which is `C^n` for all `n`, but not `C^∞`. We solve this issue by putting locality conditions
72: in space and order in our definition of `ContDiffWithinAt` and `ContDiffOn`.
73: The resulting definition is slightly more complicated to work with (in fact not so much), but it
74: gives rise to completely satisfactory theorems.
75: 
76: For instance, with this definition, a real function which is `C^m` (but not better) on `(-1/m, 1/m)`
77: for each natural `m` is by definition `C^∞` at `0`.
78: 
79: There is another issue with the definition of `ContDiffWithinAt 𝕜 n f s x`. We can
80: require the existence and good behavior of derivatives up to order `n` on a neighborhood of `x`
81: within `s`. However, this does not imply continuity or differentiability within `s` of the function
82: at `x` when `x` does not belong to `s`. Therefore, we require such existence and good behavior on
83: a neighborhood of `x` within `s ∪ {x}` (which appears as `insert x s` in this file).
84: 
85: ## Notation
86: 
87: We use the notation `E [×n]→L[𝕜] F` for the space of continuous multilinear maps on `E^n` with
88: values in `F`. This is the space in which the `n`-th derivative of a function from `E` to `F` lives.
89: 
90: In this file, we denote `WithTop ℕ∞` with `ℕ∞ω`, `(⊤ : ℕ∞) : ℕ∞ω` with `∞` and `⊤ : ℕ∞ω` with `ω`.
91: To avoid ambiguities with the two tops, the theorem names use either `infty` or `omega`.
92: These notations are scoped in `ContDiff`.
93:

value.text: Fix x∈ℝ^n and t>0. H001 gives positive finite dimensions and H002 permits all derivatives used here. By H004, u·u=1. Differentiation in time, by the ordinary product rule for the finite component sum defining the dot product, gives 2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Choose the pointwise scalar a from H005. Then u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses no derivative or regularity of a.

Twice differentiating u·u=1 in time gives 2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt=0. For an arbitrary coordinate j0∈{1,...,n}, twice differentiating in x_{j0} similarly gives 2|∂_{x_{j0}}u|²+2u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=0. Thus u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=−|∂_{x_{j0}}u|². Generalize j0 over the spatial coordinates. Dot the normality equation for a with u and use |u|²=1. Finite distributivity and the definition of Δ_xu give a=u·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². The same calculation applies to every scalar satisfying that pointwise equation.

F001 proves the two orthogonality identities at the arbitrary point. By F002 substitute the computed value of a into the pointwise normality equation from H005 to obtain u_tt−Δ_xu=(Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|²)u. The scalar was chosen only at this point and is eliminated; it is not promoted to a regular scalar field. Generalizing x and t proves all the asserted pointwise identities.
Fix t0>0 and set J=[t0/2,3t0/2]. Both endpoints are positive and the first is strictly smaller than the second. Apply H006 to these two times to obtain a compact set outside which u=q throughout J.

Choose such a compact C from F001. Compact subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space are bounded: for example the increasing family of open boxes with positive integral radii covers C, and a finite subcover puts C in one such box. Enlarging its radius if needed gives a positive radius with strict containment in the open box. This also covers C empty.

Choose R as in F002 and set Q=[−R,R]^n. Its Lebesgue measure is (2R)^n<∞. The complement of compact C is open. On the open set (ℝ^n∖C)×int J the map u is the constant q by F001. H002 implies that all positive-order derivatives vanish on that open set. Thus at interior times e, e_t and the products u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every j vanish outside C. Products and finite sums of smooth derivatives are continuous; in particular e and e_t are jointly continuous on the original open space-time domain.

At any r∈int J, each spatial function in question is continuous, hence Lebesgue measurable, and bounded on compact Q. Its absolute value is bounded by a finite nonnegative constant times the indicator of Q, since it vanishes outside C⊂Q. The integral of that bound is the constant times (2R)^n, which is finite. This proves absolute integrability of e(·,r), e_t(·,r), u_t·u_tt, ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t, u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u, and ∂_{x_j}(u_t·∂_{x_j}u), for every spatial index j. No interchange of a derivative and an integral is used here.

Since t0∈int J, F004 in particular proves integrability of e(·,t0). Generalize the arbitrary t0 and existentially retain the compatible C,R and their box Q, together with F001–F004, to obtain the full quantified support and integrability assertion. Joint continuity of e and e_t was established in S003 using H002. The energy integral has therefore been proved finite at every positive time, before introducing the finite energy function.

value.text: Fix t0>0 and take J,C,R,Q from N002 at this t0. The guarded definition E is now available. By H001 and H002, the finite product rule and equality of mixed spatial and time derivatives give, at all x and positive t, e_t(x,t)=2u_t(x,t)·u_tt(x,t)+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u(x,t)·∂_{x_j}u_t(x,t). The products and e_t are integrable at every positive time by N002.

Set η=t0/4. Then η>0 and [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J. Joint continuity of e_t from N002 on the compact set Q×[t0−η,t0+η] gives a finite nonnegative upper bound for |e_t| there. Indeed its continuous absolute value has a bounded compact image in ℝ.

Choose B0 from F002. For arbitrary x and 0<|h|<η, apply M004 to the real function r↦e(x,r), with derivative r↦e_t(x,r), on the closed interval whose endpoints are min(t0,t0+h) and max(t0,t0+h). Smoothness gives continuity and the indicated derivative on that interval; all times lie in [t0−η,t0+η]. If a total function on ℝ is required, set it to zero at nonpositive times; this leaves this positive interval and its local derivatives unchanged. For x∈Q, M004 and F002 imply |(e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0))/h|≤B0. This is the same slope in either ordering of the endpoints. For x∉Q both densities vanish by N002, so the quotient is zero. Thus the uniform dominating function on ℝ^n is B0·1_Q, where 1_Q is one on Q and zero off Q. It is integrable since Q is measurable of finite measure.

Fix an arbitrary sequence hseq:ℕ→ℝ. Temporarily assume L1: for every k, 0<|hseq(k)|<η and hseq(k)→0. Define Fseq(k)(x)=[e(x,t0+hseq(k))−e(x,t0)]/hseq(k). Each Fseq(k) is continuous in x and hence almost everywhere strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure. F003 gives the bound |Fseq(k)(x)|≤B0·1_Q(x) for every k and x. The definition of the time derivative gives Fseq(k)(x)→e_t(x,t0) at every x, because hseq tends to zero through nonzero increments. All Fseq(k) are integrable, by the bound or by integrability of their two densities.

Apply M001 with measurable space ℝ^n, Lebesgue measure, codomain ℝ, sequence Fseq, limit x↦e_t(x,t0), and bound B0·1_Q. F003 and F004 verify all premises. It follows that ∫Fseq(k) dx→∫e_t(x,t0) dx. Since both densities are integrable by N002, linearity of the real Lebesgue integral identifies the left integral with [E(t0+hseq(k))−E(t0)]/hseq(k).

Discharge L1: F005 holds for every sequence of nonzero increments tending to zero and having absolute value less than η. This proves the full punctured limit as the increment tends to zero: otherwise one could choose, in successively smaller punctured neighborhoods of zero, increments whose energy quotients stay a fixed positive distance from ∫e_t(x,t0)dx. Such a sequence tends to zero and lies in that same increment range, contradicting F005. Thus E is differentiable at t0 with E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0) dx. Together with F001, and generalization of arbitrary t0, this proves the full asserted differentiability formula and its integrability clauses. Neither the chosen support witnesses nor the test sequence escapes this conclusion.

Fix t0>0 and j∈{1,...,n}, and choose compatible J,C,R,Q from N002 at t0. Define g(x)=u_t(x,t0)·∂_{x_j}u(x,t0). It is smooth by H002. It is zero off C by N002. Since the compact C lies in int Q, there is a neighborhood of ∂Q disjoint from C (and if C is empty all these functions are zero everywhere). Therefore g vanishes on a neighborhood of ∂Q. The product rule gives ∂_{x_j}g=∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u+u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u at time t0. All three derivative integrands are integrable by N002.

Let Qrest=[−R,R]^(n−1), and let T(y,z) insert z into coordinate j, keeping the other coordinates in their original order. Set Hfun(y,z)=∂_{x_j}g(T(y,z)). The coordinate permutation identifies Q with Qrest×[−R,R] and Lebesgue integration on Q with integration for the product of Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest and Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R]. This follows from the Cartesian product definition of Euclidean Lebesgue measure: rectangles have the product of their side lengths, invariant under coordinate reordering; that determines this measure. If n=1 the remaining factor ℝ^0 is a singleton with mass one, so the same identification applies. Both restricted measures are finite, hence s-finite. Hfun is continuous and bounded on this compact product; the product measure is finite, so Hfun is integrable there. For each fixed y∈Qrest, z↦g(T(y,z)) is smooth with derivative Hfun(y,z). Its derivative is bounded on [−R,R], hence interval integrable, and its endpoint values are zero by F001.

For arbitrary y∈Qrest apply M003 with codomain ℝ, endpoints −R,R, f(z)=g(T(y,z)), and derivative d(z)=Hfun(y,z). R>0 and F002 give the ordering, continuity, derivative and integrability premises. It follows that ∫_{−R}^{R}Hfun(y,z) dz=g(T(y,R))−g(T(y,−R))=0. Since endpoints have one-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero, the interval integral equals the integral for Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R]. Generalize y.

Apply M002 to Hfun with outer measure Lebesgue measure restricted to Qrest and inner measure Lebesgue measure restricted to [−R,R], codomain ℝ. F002 proves product integrability and s-finiteness. The iterated integral is zero by F003. Fubini therefore gives zero for the product integral, and the coordinate identification in F002 gives ∫_Q ∂_{x_j}g dx=0. This holds also in the singleton outer factor when n=1.

By F001 the derivative and both product summands vanish outside Q, so their whole-space integrals equal their integrals over Q. Integrate the product identity in F001, using absolute integrability and linearity. F004 gives 0=∫_{ℝ^n}∂_{x_j}u_t·∂_{x_j}u dx+∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx, at time t0. Symmetry of the Euclidean dot product gives the asserted identity with ∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t on the left. Generalize t0 and j to obtain the asserted integration-by-parts identity, including the integrability clauses.

Fix t0>0. N002 proves integrability of e(·,t0) and of all product terms below, so E is the actual finite integral. N003 proves its differentiability and gives E'(t0)=∫e_t(x,t0) dx with e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_{j=1}^n∂_{x_j}u·∂_{x_j}u_t. Substitute this identity, use linearity and interchange the finite sum and integral (H001 gives a finite dimension), and apply N004 to each j. This yields E'(t0)=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·u_tt dx−2Σ_{j=1}^n∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·∂_{x_jx_j}u dx=2∫_{ℝ^n}u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu) dx, all fields evaluated at t0.

By N001 the final integrand in F001 is zero at every x, so E'(t0)=0. Since t0 was arbitrary, N002 and N003 together prove the complete target: e(·,t) is integrable and E is differentiable with E'(t)=0 for every positive t. No time-zero value or limiting assertion is used.

To retain the final conservation statement of the supplied proof, fix s,t>0. If s<t, apply M004 to E and the zero derivative on [s,t]; extend E by zero to nonpositive times solely to match the source's total domain. F002 gives differentiability and hence continuity at all points of this positive closed interval, and derivative zero in its interior. The theorem gives slope zero and therefore E(t)=E(s). If t<s use the same application with the endpoints interchanged, and if s=t equality is immediate. Thus E is constant on (0,∞). This retains exactly the exercise's normalization.

119: ### 4. Integration by parts and cancellation
120: 
121: For each spatial index \(j\), at time \(t_0\) put
122: \(g_j(x)=u_t(x,t_0)\cdot\partial_{x_j}u(x,t_0)\).
123: It is smooth and vanishes on a neighborhood of the boundary of \(Q\),
124: because \(C\subset\operatorname{int}Q\). The product rule gives
125: 
126: \[
127: \partial_{x_j}g_j
128: =\partial_{x_j}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_j}u
129:  +u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u.
130: \]
131: 
132: Integrate first over \(x_j\in[-R,R]\) at fixed remaining coordinates.
133: The fundamental theorem of calculus gives zero because both endpoint
134: values of \(g_j\) are zero. Fubini applies on \(Q\) because the
135: derivative and its two summands are continuous and bounded on a
136: finite-measure box. Thus \(\int_Q\partial_{x_j}g_j=0\).
137: All these terms vanish outside \(Q\), so
138: 
139: \[
140: \int_{\mathbb R^n}\partial_{x_j}u\cdot\partial_{x_j}u_t\,dx
141: =-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx.              \tag{4}
142: \]
143: 
144: Every integral is finite by step 2. Sum (4) over the finitely many
145: spatial indices and substitute (2) into (3):
146: 
147: \[
148: \begin{aligned}
149: E'(t_0)
150: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot u_{tt}\,dx
151:  -2\sum_{j=1}^n\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot\partial_{x_jx_j}u\,dx\\
152: &=2\int_{\mathbb R^n}u_t\cdot(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu)\,dx=0,
153: \end{aligned}
154: \]
155: 
156: by (1). This holds at every \(t_0>0\). Hence \(E\) is differentiable
157: with zero derivative on \((0,\infty)\), and is constant there by the
158: mean value theorem. This is conservation of energy with exactly the
159: normalization in the exercise.

8: abbrev X (n : ℕ) := Fin n → ℝ

11: def domain (n : ℕ) : Set (X n × ℝ) := {p | 0 < p.2}

13:   Set.pi Set.univ (fun _ => Set.Icc (-R) R)

16: def slab (t : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Set.Icc (t / 2) (3 * t / 2)

18: noncomputable def dt {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) : X n × ℝ → V m :=
19:   fun p => deriv (fun r : ℝ => u (p.1, r)) p.2
20: noncomputable def dx {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) (j : Fin n) :
21:     X n × ℝ → V m :=
22:   fun p => fderiv ℝ (fun x : X n => u (x, p.2)) p.1 (Pi.single j 1)

24:   fun p => ∑ j : Fin n, dx (dx u j) j p
25: noncomputable def density {n m : ℕ} (u : X n × ℝ → V m) :
